subject: Matemática
description_pt: Compreender os processos de fatoração de expressões algébricas, com base em suas relações com os produtos notáveis, para resolver e elaborar problemas que possam ser representados por equações polinomiais do 2º grau.

components.description_pt: Identificar expressões algébricas que podem ser fatoradas usando padrões de produtos notáveis
components.description_en: Identify algebraic expressions that can be factored using notable product patterns
components.cc_component_description: Identify algebraic or geometric structure to simplify or solve a complex expression

components.description_pt: Identificar quando uma equação quadrática é melhor resolvida por fatoração e fatorar para resolver
components.description_en: Identify when a quadratic equation is best solved through factoring and factor to solve the equation
components.cc_component_description: Identify when a quadratic equation is best solved through factoring and factor to solve the equation

components.description_pt: Compor um problema representável por uma equação polinomial de segundo grau usando fatoração
components.description_en: Compose a problem representable by a second-degree polynomial equation using factoring
components.cc_component_description: Create polynomial equations in one variable in a contextual situation

cc_matches.description: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for $x^{2} = 49$), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.
Look for and make use of structure.

Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it. *For example, see $x_{4} — y_{4}$ as $(x^{2})^{2} — (y^{2})^{2}$, thus recognizing it as a difference of squares that can be factored as $(x^{2} — y^{2})(x^{2} + y^{2})$.*
Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.
